title: The key set of the decision entry of an agent step, the sub-decision code beside the route code, and the field set of the two ledger reads have no source
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031 and T3.2 LOV-DECISION; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-P7-001-02; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-08; legacy RWB-TE-013 sections 4 step 8 and 12
section: Sections 1, 4, 7 (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC8), 11, 12.1 and 12.4 of the story
description: Three values are not fixed by any source: (1) the key set of the actions jsonb of a decision entry written for an agent step - no column of TSD P7 v2 T3.1 holds the agent run id, the autonomy mode or the fallback reason, and no source says whether they are new columns or members of actions (DF-DEC-014); (2) which sub-decision code an agent step writes - LOV-DECISION is not enumerated in T3.2, the route agent sits in decision D6 of Architecture v5 slide 17 step 5, and the fixtures carry D6 while no source defines a sub-decision such as D6.1 for an agent step; (3) the request and answer field set of API-P7-006 and API-P7-007 beyond the fields T-A.2 names, and the field set of the ledger record on rwb.decision-record.v1 beyond the four fields of EV-08 (entryId, caseId, decisionCode, approver).
evidence: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 lists DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031 with no agent run, mode or reason column and types actions as the jsonb DF-DEC-014; TSD P7 v2 T3.2 gives LOV-DECISION by name only; T-A.2 gives the query as caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page and size and names DecisionLogPage and DecisionLogEntry without their field set; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-08 names the four legacy fields; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.4.2 AC-ALT-P7-001-02 names the seven field groups of an entry and none of the agent facts; legacy RWB-TE-013 section 4 step 8 writes actions fallback true with reason TIMED_OUT and section 12 names no column.
area: P7 decision record: entry payload, decision code and read field sets
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the P10 agent runtime business analyst and the data steward
proposed: At the design review of wave 1 the solution architect, the P10 business analyst and the data steward approve, in the OpenAPI of the service and in the physical schema, the actions key set of an agent-step entry, the decision code an agent step writes as a value of LOV-DECISION, and the request and answer field set of the two reads; until then the story holds the reading of ASM-B-P7-05-TE013-1 and the fixtures carry D6

title: The operation and parameter names of the agent fallback-rate measure have no source
source: Legacy RWB-TE-013 section 2 (fallback rate target below 10 percent per month); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (P9 owns measures and snapshots) and slide 28; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.1
section: Sections 2, 4 step 11, 7 (AC8), 8 (BR11), 12.1 and 13 of the story
description: The legacy story measures the agent fallback rate below 10 percent per month but no source names the measure definition, the reporting operation that serves it, or the parameter rows that hold its target and its window. The measure itself belongs to rwb-reporting under Arch v5 slide 41, and this story only makes the facts countable: the agent version on every entry that had one and the fallback fact in its actions. The names of the measure and of its parameters are not fixed, and the story therefore writes no name.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-013 section 2 gives the target and section 7 AC2 to AC4 write the fallback fact; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P9 the measures and snapshots and slide 28 the measure publish; TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 has no measure operation; no source lists a parameter row for a fallback target or window; Template and Rules v1 R3 puts parameters with rwb-case (DP-06).
area: Agent fallback measure and its parameters, P9 rwb-reporting with P3 rwb-case
owner_role: Data steward with the P9 reporting analyst and the P10 agent runtime business analyst
proposed: The measure definition, its target and its window are approved as rwb-reporting rows and its parameters as rwb-case parameter rows at the measures review of wave 1; until then the story asserts only that the fallback fact and the agent version are on the entry, so the measure can be defined without a change to the ledger

title: The text of MSG-P7-009 and the shape of an append that is refused are not written out in any source
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.2.4.2 and A2.2.4.3 (MSG-P7-009 named, text not given); TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T-A.2; legacy RWB-TE-013 sections 5 X4 and 14 (MSG-P7-003 only)
section: Sections 4 step 8, 5, 7 (AC6), 12.4 and 14 of the story
description: MSG-P7-009 is named by the FSD P7 flows and its text is never written out; no source fixes what the answer carries when the ingest refuses a record - whether the refusal names the field, whether the record is held for a retry and a dead-letter path, whether an alert is raised, and what the producer sees. This story answers a refused record with MSG-P7-009 naming the field and holds it for the retry and dead-letter path with an alert, and nothing is added to the ledger, but that shape is a reading and not a source value.
evidence: FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.2 and A2.2.4.3 name MSG-P7-009 without its text; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 fixes 422 as a validation answer with a problem response but not the refusal of an ingest; legacy RWB-TE-013 section 5 names MSG-P7-003 for a failed write and the word SCHEMA for a guardrail failure, and section 14 lists four message ids none of which is MSG-P7-009.
area: P7 message set and the refused append of the decision ledger
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the platform event team
proposed: The text of MSG-P7-009 and the retry, dead-letter and alert treatment of a refused record are approved with the message catalogue of wave 1 and published with the topic contract; until then the story holds the reading of ASM-B-P7-05-TE013-3 and no criterion depends on the wording

title: The name of the per-service database login is not fixed by any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20, 41 and 45; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1
description: Architecture v5 gives every service its own schema and its own login, but no source fixes the login name of rwb-decision. The story therefore writes the phrase the rwb-decision login (DP-02) and never a name, and no migration, script or test carries one.
evidence: Architecture v5 slides 20, 41 and 45 give each of the 19 services a schema rwb_name and a DB login without naming the login; Template and Rules v1 DP-02 fixes one login per service; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 names the schema only.
area: ACE DB login allocation, P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: ACE DB team with the platform team
proposed: The login name is allocated with the schema at the P7 DB story of RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and written into the platform secret store; the story keeps the phrase and needs no change when the name arrives

title: The DP table adds platform and published dependencies that the metadata rows of the story do not carry
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-11, DP-15, DP-19 and DP-20; R5.4 dependency classes; the metadata rows Depends on (build) = None and Contract dependencies = RWB-P10-TE013-CON
section: Section 13 (pattern application), section 12.2 and the metadata table of the story
description: The DP rows this story applies add dependencies absent from its metadata: H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03), H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON (DP-04), H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON (DP-07), H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (DP-09), H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (DP-10), H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (DP-15) and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON (DP-19). The authorise answer of rwb-access consumed by the two reads is also outside the Ownership Map API table, so it is carried here with them. The metadata names only RWB-P10-TE013-CON, which is the DP-20 agent contract.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5: DP-03 H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; DP-04 H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON; DP-07 H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON; DP-09 H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; DP-10 H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; DP-15 H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; DP-19 H RWB-PLT-N001-CON; DP-20 C RWB-P10-TE013-CON; ownership.json has no row for a POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise permission decision.
area: Dependency map and build sequencing, P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: Solution architect, P7 rwb-decision, with the platform team and the rwb-case and rwb-access teams
proposed: Carry the seven platform H dependencies, the three published C dependencies and the P4 authorise answer in the dependency map as DP-added, keep Ready to start at Day 1 because every H is a platform CON story and every C is built against its published contract and fake, and correct the metadata rows at the next version of the story set

title: No source fixes the model version of agent INTAKE, which the entry must carry
source: Legacy RWB-TE-013 sections 3, 4 step 8 and 7 AC1; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 (agent policy and run); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (P10 owns policies, prompts, runs)
description: The entry carries the model version of the run, and the legacy story names a model version only for another agent. The agent INTAKE of the fixtures has a policy P1, a prompt PR1 and the agent version INTAKE@P1/PR1, but no model version, and this story may not invent one: the value is a P10 fact that arrives inside the record.
evidence: Legacy RWB-TE-013 section 3 gives the policy P1 and its timeout and section 7 AC1 writes the agent version INTAKE@P1/PR1 with no model version; FSD P10 v3 keeps the model version on the run; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P10 the policies, prompts and runs; the story therefore reads the model version from the record and asserts only that it is present.
area: Agent run facts consumed by the P7 decision record, P10 rwb-agent
owner_role: P10 agent runtime business analyst with the model risk officer
proposed: The model version of agent INTAKE is fixed with the approved policy of the agent in RWB-P10-TE013-CON and RWB-P10-TE013-APP and arrives inside the record; the fixtures of this story carry a synthetic model version and the criteria assert presence, not a value
